questions.q_en: What was the actual growth rate of the first five-year plan?

questions.q_en: Which Five Year Plan period saw the initiation of the Hill Area Development Programme?
questions.solution_en:
The Hill Area Development Programme (HADP) was initiated during the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979). The program aimed at the socio-economic development of designated hill areas, focusing on ecological balance and sustainable development.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-1985)

• Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974): Some pilot projects for hill areas might have started, but the formal HADP is associated with the Fifth Plan.

• Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-1997)

Further insights:

• The HADP covered specific hill areas in states like Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh (now Uttarakhand), and the Western Ghats region.

• The program focused on sectors like agriculture, horticulture, forestry, soil conservation, animal husbandry, and development of infrastructure.

• It recognized the unique geographical and ecological challenges faced by hill regions.

Aimed to transform India from an agrarian to an industrial economy

Mahalanobis was a key economic advisor to Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru

ii. The First Five-Year Plan laid emphasis on agriculture development.

iii. The First Five-Year Plan model in india was borrowed from Russia.
questions.solution_en:
· Statement i is incorrect: The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) was not based on the P.C. Mahalanobis model. Instead, it was inspired by the Harrod-Domar model, which focused on capital formation and investment. The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis model, which emphasized heavy industries and economic self-reliance.

· Statement ii is correct: The First Five-Year Plan focused on agricultural development to achieve food self-sufficiency. The major projects under this plan included the Bhakra-Nangal Dam and Hirakud Dam.

· Statement iii is correct: The planning model for the First Five-Year Plan in India was inspired by Russia (Soviet Union), which had a centralized economic planning system. However, the Indian model was adapted to suit its own economic conditions.

Thus, the correct answer is A. Only ii and iii.

questions.q_en:
P.C. Mahalanobis is remembered as a major contributor to India's developmental path because he:

(A) Set up the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs)

(B) Formulated the Second Five-Year Plan

(C) Was the first Minister of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.solution_en:
· Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, an Indian statistician, is best known for formulating the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961).

· This plan was based on the Mahalanobis Model, which emphasized heavy industries and rapid economic growth.

· He was the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) and played a crucial role in developing statistical methods for economic planning.

· His work in statistics also led to the Mahalanobis Distance, a measure used in data science and classification problems.

· He is often called the "Father of Indian Statistics."

Misconception: While he contributed to India's educational development, he did not set up IIMs, nor was he a Minister of Statistics.

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements is correct?.
options_en: The five-year plan focuses mostly on private intervention in the economy.
The five-year plan always focused on the growth of the tertiary sector.
The five-year plan permits long-term intervention by the government in the economy.
A five-year plan always stresses market-oriented activities.
questions.solution_en:
Statement 1: Incorrect. Five-year plans in India focused on government intervention to promote balanced economic development, especially in key sectors like agriculture, industry, and infrastructure.

Statement 2: Correct. The five-year plans were designed to allow long-term government intervention to achieve planned economic goals, including reducing poverty, boosting industrial and agricultural production, and addressing social inequities.

Statement 3: Incorrect. While some plans emphasized the tertiary sector (services), they also focused on primary (agriculture) and secondary (industry) sectors, depending on the priorities of the plan.

Statement 4: Incorrect. The five-year plans were not solely market-oriented; they followed a mixed economy model, combining market mechanisms with government planning and regulation.

questions.q_en: In which five-year plan was the 'food, work, and productivity' slogan used?
questions.solution_en:
The 'food, work, and productivity' slogan was used in the Seventh Five-Year Plan of India.

Five-Year Plans in India are detailed macroeconomic plans created by the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) to guide economic development. The Seventh Five-Year Plan, which ran from 1985 to 1990, emphasized economic growth, agricultural productivity, and employment generation.

The slogan "food, work, and productivity" reflected the plan's focus on addressing basic economic needs, creating employment opportunities, and improving overall economic efficiency.
